entries.passageText: Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in the remembrance of Allah. Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!
entries.reflection: Hearts are restless by nature, pulled by worry and noise. This verse names where rest is found: in the remembrance of Allah. Even a brief remembrance between tasks can return the heart to calm.
studyPrompts: What is unsettling your heart most today?
When during your day could you pause for remembrance?
How have you experienced calm through prayer or dhikr before?

entries.passageText: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing.
entries.reflection: Moses and Aaron were sent on a daunting mission and admitted their fear. Allah's answer was not that the task was easy, but that He was with them, hearing and seeing. Courage grows from knowing you are not unseen.
studyPrompts: What task in front of you feels daunting?
How does knowing Allah hears and sees change how you approach it?
Who could you support as they face something difficult?

entries.passageText: And will provide for him from (a quarter) whence he hath no expectation. And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him. Lo! Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah hath set a measure for all things.
entries.reflection: Worry often comes from trying to carry every outcome ourselves. This verse reminds the believer that provision can come from where we least expect, and that Allah suffices whoever puts their trust in Him. Do your part, then let the weight of the outcome rest with Him.
studyPrompts: Which outcome are you trying hardest to control right now?
What does putting your trust in Allah look like alongside doing your duty well?
When has help come to you from an unexpected place?

entries.passageText: And have appointed your sleep for repose, And have appointed the night as a cloak, And have appointed the day for livelihood.
entries.reflection: Sleep, night, and day are named here as gifts, each with its purpose. Rest is part of the design, not a weakness. When duty allows, receive sleep as a mercy rather than time lost.
studyPrompts: How are you sleeping and resting lately?
What keeps you from receiving rest as a gift?
How could you better balance work and rest this week?

entries.passageText: Therefore remember Me, I will remember you. Give thanks to Me, and reject not Me.
entries.reflection: Remembrance and gratitude are tied together here: remember Allah and He remembers you; give thanks and do not be ungrateful. Gratitude keeps blessings in view when circumstances are hard. Today, name a few blessings you might otherwise overlook.
studyPrompts: What blessings have you overlooked recently?
How does being remembered by Allah encourage you?
How could you express thanks to the people around you today?

entries.passageText: But lo! with hardship goeth ease, Lo! with hardship goeth ease;
entries.reflection: The promise is repeated so that it is not missed: with hardship goes ease. Ease does not only come after hardship; it comes with it. Look for the small ease within today's difficulty.
studyPrompts: What hardship are you facing right now?
What ease, however small, can you find within it?
Why do you think this promise is repeated?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast.
entries.reflection: Steadfastness and prayer are offered as the two supports for hard times. Allah is with the steadfast, so patience is never endured alone. Keeping prayer even in a demanding schedule is itself an act of steadfastness.
studyPrompts: Where do you most need steadfastness right now?
How does prayer help you carry what is hard?
What would help you keep your prayers during a busy or irregular schedule?

entries.passageText: And verily whoso is patient and forgiveth - lo! that, verily, is (of) the steadfast heart of things.
entries.reflection: Patience and forgiveness are described here as the steadfast heart of things, not as weakness. In close quarters, small wrongs happen often. Choosing to forgive is a strength that keeps a unit, and a heart, intact.
studyPrompts: Is there someone you find it hard to forgive right now?
How is forgiveness a form of strength?
What would patience look like in a relationship that tests you?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do.
entries.reflection: This verse asks for justice even when it costs us or those we love. Integrity means the truth does not change depending on who benefits. It names personal desire as the thing that pulls us away from fairness.
studyPrompts: Where are you tempted to bend the truth for yourself or someone close to you?
What helps you stay fair when your own interests are involved?
What does it mean to be a witness for Allah in your daily work?

entries.passageText: And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright.
entries.reflection: Allah answers the question before it is fully asked: I am near. No distance from home, family, or community puts a believer out of reach of His hearing. Call on Him from wherever you are tonight.
studyPrompts: When do you feel most alone?
What would you like to say to Allah tonight?
How can you stay connected to your faith community while far from home?
